summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with chronic pancreatitis, depression, anxiety, and a history of venous thrombosis, was admitted for an acute exacerbation of chronic pancreatitis characterized by severe epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake. She was managed with IV fluids, IV pain medications including Toradol and Dilaudid, and antiemetics per her established outpatient protocol. Her symptoms gradually improved, allowing transition to oral tramadol and a regular diet. Blood pressure was elevated on admission, likely due to pain and missed medications, and was managed by restarting lisinopril and increasing amlodipine from 5mg to 10mg daily. IV pantoprazole was used temporarily and switched back to oral omeprazole. She remained mentally stable on home seroquel and amitriptyline. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up instructions for blood pressure monitoring and primary care.
